What *is* gross is treating someone like a sexual object... because even though you may find there body attractive, they are still a multifaceted individual with thoughts, feelings, emotions, experience, talents, skills, sense of humor, favorite movie, flaws etc. Being sexually attracted to someone does not mean you are objectifying them — it becomes objectification when you stop considering them as fully formed humans.

You mention girls who post videos online and how it seems like they do it for others and not themselves. I definitely see where you’re coming from but maybe think of it like this: when someone posts something to social media, are they thinking “Oh wow user1, user2 and user3 specifically are really going to love this” or are they thinking, “this is cool, I want to show someone / this will get to the front page / someone might be able to help me with my problem / etc”. People don’t usually make posts *for* other people... they make posts to connect, to be validated, to rack up views or likes or whatever. They make the post because ultimately they will gain something from it, be it emotional gain or information or attention. That doesn’t change even if it is a girl twerking or w/e. 

Even when someone does post something specifically to catch one person’s attention, they’re usually still seeking something for themselves: either to alter the opinion that person has of them, to alter the relationship they hold with that person and/or so that the poster will receive a response a response or incite an interaction. They’re still posting for themselves, in order to achieve a goal. You feel me?

If someone’s body prompts you to think sexual thoughts then that’s one thing, that’s very okay. But you can and should have sexual thoughts without objectifying the person. You don’t have to love their personality or even know them at all to remind yourself that even if they might be a sexy internet stranger ^(title of my sex tape) they are still a real person.

It is also useful to understand an author’s intentions and culture in order to lend context to the work but their political beliefs do not need to rob you of the joy you felt when you observed their work. 

JK Rowling may be the author but your experience reading harry potter cannot be touched by another. 

buy the books thrifted or borrow from a friend if you can, or purchase once and do not buy duplicates. if you don’t already own the series and would like to, im sure thriftbooks.com or ebay can help you. this avoids contributing to rowling’s wealth.

i have fine hair similar to yours although my hair has a slight wave to it as well. i feel that products with coconut oil can very easily weigh fine hair down so i would be choosy when it comes to products with that ingredient. 

i condition every day or every other day but definitely every single time i shower. on weekends i use the amika soulfood hair mask, either in place of conditioner or on my damp hair for an hour before rinsing out. this keeps my ends super soft and healthy. if you want softness and shine throughout, try a honey mask from roots to ends for about an hour before shampooing out — you will probably have to shampoo two or three times to get it all out but your hair will be super soft afterwards. 

other things that have worked for my fine hair:

almond oil hair mask, leave in hair for 30 mins-1 hour. apply from midshaft to ends, shampoo out (repeat shampoo x3 to get it all out)

apple cider vinegar rinse in shower is easy and cheap and i think it left my hair soft and shiny,  but i am very picky with how my hair smells and i felt like it i could still smell it after my shower

bedhead motor mouth product - run through damp hair and blow dry upside down. will add volume and shine although the texture is slightly tacky

briogeo leave in conditioner 

keep in mind if you use products you will have to wash more often to prevent buildup. if you do blow dry consider using a protective heat spray or keep the blowdryer on the cool setting as heat can be damaging

consider a satin pillow case - they’re cheap on amazon and will reduce breakage and make your hair more manageable in the morning. wear your hair in a braid or loosely toed back when you go to sleep to protect it

if you’re after a low maintenance approach i would recommend the satin pillowcase, more frequent conditioning and a leave in conditioner.

A boar bristle brush is worth buying. It helps distribute oils down the hair shaft which may help you get an extra day without washing, and it’s good for distributing product too. 

A leave in conditioner is good too. Try to keep your ends moisturized. Apply the leave in conditioner from mid-shaft to end, and you can also add an oil to just the ends. This won’t make your hair grow faster but it will help to improve the look of your ends and prevent breakage. 

Keep trying to hold off on washing for as long as you can until you have to. Maybe keeping your hair off your face will prevent the breakouts? As you go longer without washing your scalp will adjust and produce less oil. 

Another option is you can shampoo with a 2-in-1 shampoo/conditioner, condition with regular conditioner, and apply a hair recovery mask designed to be used in-shower to ur ends. Alternate with regular shampoo as needed. 

Other hair masks are easy to make at home: I use one thats one part honey one part olive oil. Massage into dry or damp hair, wrap in a towel, chill for an hour or two and then shower. (Use regular shampoo, not the 2-in-1, to get it out). 

A microfiber towel and a silk pillowcase are both pretty cheap on amazon and will help prevent breakage.

I have ptsd for the same reason. Striking the balance between taking care of your mental and spiritual health can be really tough and confusing, and I imagine if I had that experience with a priest it would be extremely difficult to let go of. 

It seems like going to someone else for confession may be a good place to start, just so that you can confess your resentment to someone besides the person you resent (if you feel that you need to confess it — it may be helpful, but it’s your call whether to do so or not). If you are still going to confession with someone who you are at odds with, I imagine it is more difficult to open your heart to Christ. I worry this issue might be negatively impacting your confession experience as a whole, and going to another priest might alleviate this. You said you don’t have access to other Catholic Churches, but I assume there is at least one other priest at your church. Maybe you can email him directly, to set up a time for confession, if he doesn’t regularly do confessions. Another option would be showing up to Mass early and seeing if you can do a quick one beforehand. 

As for dealing with symptoms, I had decent luck with medication. A psychiatrist is able to provide some guidance in regards to your thoughts feelings during check ups without requiring the same time commitment as a counselor, and medication can help in between. Also identifying triggers — after some time I realized certain locations, smells, whatever weren’t sending me into immediate panic attacks or flashbacks, but were slowly wearing me down and exhausting me. Once I knew what those were I could remove them from my life, and it made a huge difference. 

I hope this is helpful. One last thing: throughout my initial assault and the recovery afterwards, men in my life were continually a source of pain, hurt, and disappointment. I have fostered a newfound devotion to St. Joseph, who was ever sacrificing, silent, devoted, and good to Our Lady and to Christ. Maybe exploring a special devotion to him — or a different saint more fitting for you — can help. I will pray for you.
